english_translation: Please show me the way to the nearest clinic.

dialogue.shona: Ndinokumbira undiratidze nzira inoenda kukiriniki iri pedyo.
dialogue.english: Please show me the way to the nearest clinic.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Ndinokumbira [I kumbira] • undiratidze [undiratidze] • nzira [nzira] • inoenda [it enda] • kukiriniki [to / at kiriniki] • iri [iri] • pedyo [pedyo]

grammar_notes.title: Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('Ndinokumbira')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'Ndinokumbira' uses the present marker '-no-'. In Shona, inserting '-no-' between the subject prefix and the verb stem expresses general truths, everyday habits, or states of mind like 'wanting', 'thinking', and 'knowing'. For example: 'ndinoda' ('I want/like'), 'unofunga' ('you think'), 'vanoti' ('they say'), and 'vanorima' ('they farm').
grammar_notes.rule: [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)

grammar_notes.title: Talking About Location: 'pa-', 'ku-', and 'mu-' ('pedyo')
grammar_notes.content:
Look at how location is expressed with 'pedyo'. Instead of separate prepositions like 'on', 'to', or 'in', Shona attaches one of three location prefixes directly to the front of a noun:
• 'pa-' means 'at' or 'on' a specific point or surface (e.g., 'patafura' = on the table, 'pamusika' = at the market, 'pasi' = on the ground).
• 'ku-' means 'to', 'from', or 'at' a general destination (e.g., 'kuchikoro' = to school, 'kumusha' = to the rural home, 'kubasa' = at/to work).
• 'mu-' means 'inside' an enclosed space (e.g., 'mumba' = inside the house, 'muguta' = in the city, 'mumugwagwa' = in the road).
grammar_notes.rule: pa- = on / at a point (patafura) | ku- = to / at a place (kuchikoro) | mu- = inside (mumba)

grammar_notes.title: Pointing Out Things: Demonstratives ('iri' = 'this / that / here')
grammar_notes.content: In Shona, words for 'this/these' and 'that/those' (like 'iri') come AFTER the noun they point to and mirror the noun's group! Near demonstratives ('this / these / right here') repeat the noun class vowel: 'mwana uyu' (this child), 'nyama iyi' (this meat), 'kapu iyi' (this cup), 'bhuku iri' (this book), 'zvinhu izvi' (these things). Replacing the final vowel with '-o' shifts the meaning to 'that / those / there': 'uyo' (that person), 'iyo' (that one), 'uko' (over there).
grammar_notes.rule: Noun + Near Demonstrative ('uyu/iyi/iri/ichi/izvi' = this/these) | replace final vowel with '-o' ('uyo/iyo/iro/icho/izvo' = that/those)

cultural_notes.title: Community Clinics ('Kiriniki') & Asking Directions in Zimbabwe
cultural_notes.content: Local health clinics ('kiriniki') serve every urban suburb and rural ward across Zimbabwe, and passersby will gladly walk part of the way with a stranger to point out the clearest path ('kuratidza nzira').

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new polite request into English: 'Chimbomirira zvishoma pamusuwo.'
options: Come inside the house and sit on the chair.
Please wait a little while at the door.
Return home early before the sun sets.
Take your books and put them in the bag.
active_exercises.correct_answer: Please wait a little while at the door.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Chimbomirira' = 'Wait a little / for a moment right now', 'zvishoma' = 'a little', 'pamusuwo' = 'at the door'.

active_exercises.prompt: You want to politely ask an elder or a group of guests to sit down ('gara'). Which imperative form should you use?
active_exercises.explanation: Adding '-i' to the verb stem ('gara' -> 'garai') forms the plural and polite command in Shona.

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Vanhu vakamira pamusika vachimirira kukwira bhazi.'
options: The driver stopped the car near the traffic lights.
We saw two large trucks carrying maize to the city.
The road to the eastern highlands has many curves.
People are standing at the market waiting to board the bus.
active_exercises.correct_answer: People are standing at the market waiting to board the bus.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Vanhu vakamira pamusika' = 'People are standing at the market', 'vachimirira kukwira bhazi' = 'waiting to board the bus'.
